list: The official 55 trophies: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze, 28 hidden. Names, descriptions and grades are reproduced exactly as PlayStation publishes them, as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles before this guide was written; the two listings agree on every name, description and grade.
notes: Guides are written for this entry in its own words. The hidden flags follow the published hidden split by grade (platinum 0 hidden, gold 1 of 2, silver 0 of 6, bronze 27 of 46, 28 in total). Story trophies are hidden; which of the remaining bronze trophies PlayStation hides is this guide's best reading of the published split, not a Rockstar confirmation. Missable status: only Positive Mental Attitude is flagged as possibly missable by published guides (PowerPyx and GTABase, unconfirmed); every other trophy is marked not-flagged, which means no source checked for this guide calls it missable, not that a miss is impossible. Time and difficulty figures in the roadmap are estimates from PowerPyx (about 200 hours, difficulty 4/10, one playthrough) and Push Square (up to 300 hours or more), labelled as estimates wherever they appear.

sources.name: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list (official names, descriptions, grades)
PSNProfiles — GTA VI trophy list coverage via Push Square
PowerPyx — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Platinum Roadmap (difficulty 4/10, about 200 hours, one playthrough, one possibly missable trophy)
GTABase — GTA 6 trophy list (hidden split, 18 meditation spots, possibly missable flag)
KeenGamer — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Platinum Roadmap (all 55 offline, single playthrough)
FullSweep — GTA 6 trophy list (12 story trophies, counts and groupings)

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum itself: it unlocks on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is nothing separate to grind for it. Plan around it instead — use the roadmap in this app, keep the possibly missable meditation trophy in mind from Chapter 1, and let A Long Road (100% completion) be the last big push, because several trophies feed into that checklist anyway. Sources: official list via Exophase and PSNProfiles; PowerPyx roadmap summary via EGamers (one playthrough, about 200 hours estimated).
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); PowerPyx roadmap via EGamers

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Gone Fishing, the opening mission of the game. It cannot be skipped: play through the introduction, learn the movement, driving and cover basics it teaches, and the trophy pops as the mission wraps up. If you are starting a platinum run, this is also the moment to switch on this tracker's spoiler shield and start the meditation habit described under Positive Mental Attitude, because the earliest meditation spot is tied to the Chapter 1 stretch of the story. Sources: official description in the Exophase / PSNProfiles list; KeenGamer roadmap, which identifies Gone Fishing as the opening mission.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 1. Simply follow the main mission markers to the chapter's end; no side content is required. Before you close the chapter out, sweep up anything chapter-bound: published guides flag the first meditation spot for Positive Mental Attitude as a Chapter 1 opportunity, so meditate whenever the game offers the prompt during this chapter rather than assuming you can walk back to it later. Keep one manual save at the chapter's start as cheap insurance. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); PowerPyx and GTABase missable note via EGamers and CryptoGames.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); PowerPyx & GTABase via EGamers / CryptoGames

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 2 — yes, the asterisks are part of the official name as PlayStation publishes it. Keep following the main story thread; chapter trophies are awarded for completion, not for medals or optional objectives, so a steady story-first pace is enough. Use the travel time between Chapter 2 missions to start habits that pay off later: discover vehicles for Whip It Good, spend in shops toward Treat Yo Self, and try any new activity type once for Master of None. Sources: official name and description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep grouping of the 12 story trophies.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep trophy list

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 3. By this point the map and the side content open up properly, so it is worth pausing the story here and there to bank activity and collectible progress while missions are still introducing you to each district. Nothing in the official description suggests a performance requirement: finish the chapter's missions in order and the trophy is yours. If a mission offers a choice, remember Actions Speak Louder tracks choices made across the whole game, so choices here still count. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); PSNProfiles chapter mapping reported by Heyday / Push Square coverage.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); Push Square / PSNProfiles via Heyday

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Story trophy for finishing Chapter 4, the last of the chapter-completion trophies before the finale arc. Treat the end of this chapter as a natural audit point: open this tracker, check off the stranger strands and activity types you have already touched, and mop up anything tied to areas the story is about to move you away from. The trophy itself only asks for chapter completion, per the official description. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap ordering of the story trophies.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The gold story trophy, awarded for completing the final mission. Before you start the finale, make a separate manual save: finales in Rockstar games tend to lock you into a sequence, and a pre-finale save is the cheapest way to revisit any endgame choice tracked by Actions Speak Louder. Go in with full health, armour and ammo, finish the mission, and the gold pops with the credits sequence. Published lists count this as the one hidden gold trophy. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); hidden-by-grade split in the EGamers and CryptoGames tables.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); EGamers / CryptoGames hidden split

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Story trophy for the named mission Breakfast Run. It sits on the main story path, so it unlocks by playing the campaign in order; there is no optional objective attached in the official description. If you are replaying for a missed collectible sweep, note that named-mission trophies like this one are the backbone of the story filter in this tracker — work through them in list order and you will never lose your place in the campaign. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep story grouping.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep trophy list

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Story trophy for completing The Cartel Heist mission. Heist-style missions usually reward preparation: stock up on armour and snacks beforehand, pick the approach the game offers that matches your loadout, and push through to the escape. Completion is all the trophy asks for. The skills it teaches — planned entry, timed escape — are the same ones the free-roam robbery trophies (Maximum Withdrawal, A Classic Blitz Play) expect later, so treat this as training. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap mission listing.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Story trophy for completing the mission Child's Play on the main path. Play the campaign in order and it unlocks at the mission's end; the official description sets no extra condition. Because several story missions sit close together in this stretch, this is a good place to keep a rotating set of manual saves — if a one-time story moment for another trophy ever worries you, a recent save is the fix. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep story grouping.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep trophy list

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Story trophy for completing the mission Headliners. Follow the main story markers, finish the mission, and the trophy unlocks automatically. No source checked for this guide attaches a score, time or stealth condition to it, so a clean completion on any approach counts. Keep pushing the story afterwards — the remaining named-mission trophies (VCIA Takedown, Operation Savage Glory) follow in the same arc. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap mission listing.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Story trophy for completing VCIA Takedown. VCIA is the airport, and it appears twice in this list: finishing this story mission is one trophy, while Catch Me If You Can asks for an unscheduled departure at the same location in free play. Do the story mission first — it teaches you the airport layout, security response and exits, which makes the free-play departure much easier to plan afterwards. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); this guide's cross-reference between the two VCIA trophies in the official list.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); cross-reference within the official list

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Story trophy for completing Operation Savage Glory, the last of the named-mission story trophies before the finale. It unlocks on mission completion like the others. After it pops, your story filter in this tracker should show only the chapter and finale trophies left — a clean signal to switch into the roadmap's clean-up stage, where side strands, activities and collectibles get finished before the final mission. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep story grouping of 12 story trophies.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep trophy list

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The long gold: reach 100% on the in-game completion checklist. Published guides agree this is the hardest and longest trophy in the set, and that the completion checklist opens up fully after the story. Work it category by category with this tracker — story, stranger strands, activities, collectibles, races, stunts and discoveries all feed the same percentage — and use the in-game checklist, not guesswork, as the source of truth for what still counts. Estimates only: PowerPyx puts the full platinum near 200 hours, Push Square's guide says up to 300 hours or more; treat both as early estimates, not measurements. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); PowerPyx estimate via EGamers; Push Square estimate via Heyday.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); PowerPyx via EGamers; Push Square via Heyday

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Bank 250 completed stunts across Leonida. Published coverage describes the stunt family broadly — stunt jumps, under-bridge flights, knife flights and base jumps all count, and you can mix them freely — so the fastest route is variety, not repeating one ramp 250 times. Clear stunt icons district by district as the story opens the map, and keep a rough tally in this tracker; stunts also feed the 100% checklist behind A Long Road, so none of the effort is wasted. Sources: official description and count (Exophase / PSNProfiles); stunt categories per FullSweep's list.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep trophy list

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample every activity type once — the official list's own starter count and published guides agree there are 9 activity types. You only have to try each one, not win it, so the moment a new activity icon appears on the map, detour and start it once. This is the cheapest bronze in the game if you do it as you explore, and the most annoying to reconstruct at the end if you did not; this tracker's activities filter shows the related trophies so you can spot which types you have already touched. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); 9 activity types per KeenGamer and FullSweep.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap; FullSweep

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold-medal every Shooting Range challenge — 42 of them, per the count carried with the official list. Treat it as a late-game trophy: accuracy and handling improve as your character stats and weapon unlocks grow, so a challenge that walls you early may fall easily later. Learn each challenge's target pattern with a silver run first, then repeat immediately while the pattern is fresh. Golds here also sharpen the gunplay that Combat Focus (Gunslinger) and the robbery trophies rely on. Sources: official description and the 42-challenge count (Exophase / PSNProfiles list data); KeenGamer roadmap.
trophies.sources: Official list + 42 count (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location — 14 locations in the official list's count. Unlike Master of None, a participation run is not enough here: you must win at each site. Drone handling is its own skill, so spend ten minutes in free flight first, learn how tightly the drone turns and how much altitude the gates allow, then run the locations in map order. Wins count per location, not in a streak, so a loss costs you nothing but time. Sources: official description and the 14-location count (Exophase / PSNProfiles list data); KeenGamer roadmap.
trophies.sources: Official list + 14 count (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different is the operative word, so farming one easy circuit 20 times does not finish it. Work the race icons as they appear across Leonida, bring a vehicle suited to each class, and do not be afraid to lower your pride and retry: only wins register. Race wins also contribute to the completion percentage for A Long Road, so this trophy is best cleared steadily during the story rather than in one endgame sitting. Sources: official description and count (Exophase / PSNProfiles); Techtroduce list summary.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); Techtroduce list summary

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing is one of the activity types, so a casual attempt also ticks a box for Master of None — but this trophy needs the win against Cal specifically. Learn the fishing loop first on ordinary spots (cast, lure, hook, manage tension), upgrade your tackle if the game offers better gear, then take Cal's challenge when your technique is steady. If he beats you, nothing is lost: challenge him again on the spot, while the spot and the rhythm of the cast are still fresh — a back-to-back rematch is the easiest version of this fight. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); activity grouping per FullSweep.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep trophy list

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish. Find an arcade cabinet in the world, pick the shortest game on offer, and play it through to its actual completion screen — quitting at a high score does not count as completing it. It also registers as one of the activity types for Master of None, so do it early while you are sampling everything once. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); activity grouping per FullSweep.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep trophy list

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's strand: work through every mission Andy gives you until his final one, then complete that too. Side strands unlock in stages as the story advances, so if Andy goes quiet, push the main story and check back. The efficient pattern for all six character trophies in this group is the same — never leave a strand half-finished when you are already in the area, because strand progress also feeds Strangers & Freaks and the 100% checklist. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); strand structure per FullSweep (14 strands in the game, 8 needed for the silver).
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep strand count

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's strand through to his final mission. As with Andy, Tyrone, Randy and Billy, the trophy is for the strand's last mission, not the first meeting, so keep returning whenever Kenton's marker reappears. Strands are staggered by story progress; if no marker shows, advance a chapter and sweep the map again. Completing strands like this one is required groundwork for the Strangers & Freaks silver. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap side-mission listing.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's strand, ending with his final mission. Keep Billy's missions on the same rotation as the other side characters: accept, complete, and check this tracker after each one so no strand silently stalls waiting on a story gate. If a strand seems finished but the trophy has not popped, you have likely only finished an intermediate mission — the strand's final mission is the one that counts. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep strangers and side-character grouping.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep trophy list

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full stranger mission strands anywhere in Leonida. Published coverage counts 14 strands in the game, so you have slack: you do not need every strand, just 8 finished ones. The named-character trophies (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are strands too, so finishing those five leaves only 3 more to find. A strand counts when its final mission is done, not when it starts — track strands, not first meetings, in this app. Sources: official description and count (Exophase / PSNProfiles); 14-strand total per PowerPyx via FullSweep.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); PowerPyx via FullSweep

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's strand through his final mission. Randy's line is one of the five named side strands that each carry their own bronze, and together they do most of the work toward the Strangers & Freaks silver. Play strands in the order the game surfaces them and revisit Randy after every story chapter — strand stages are commonly gated behind campaign progress, and a strand that looks abandoned is usually just waiting. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap side-mission listing.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's strand, ending with his final mission. Same discipline as the other character strands: complete each stage as it appears, advance the story if the strand pauses, and confirm the finish here in the tracker. With Tyrone done alongside Andy, Kenton, Billy and Randy, five of the eight strands needed for Strangers & Freaks are banked. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep strangers and side-character grouping.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep trophy list

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: POSSIBLY MISSABLE — the one trophy to plan around. Meditate at every spot in Leonida: GTABase counts 18 spots. PowerPyx and GTABase both flag this as the list's only possibly missable trophy, because the first meditation spot can be used early in the story, in Chapter 1, and it is unconfirmed whether that spot stays available afterwards; PowerPyx's author meditated there and earned the trophy, so meditating at every spot the moment the game offers it is the safe play. Do not rush Chapter 1: whenever a meditation prompt appears, use it, then keep a manual save before finishing the chapter. Everywhere else, sweep spots district by district and tick them off here. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); missable flag and Chapter 1 detail per PowerPyx and GTABase via EGamers, CryptoGames and FullSweep; 18-spot count per GTABase.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); PowerPyx & GTABase via EGamers / CryptoGames / FullSweep

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. Take Bret's request, follow the tracking steps the game gives you — unique-animal hunts in Rockstar games hinge on time of day, weather and a quiet approach — and bring the hunt to its scripted conclusion. If the animal spooks, the hunt can be re-attempted; no source checked for this guide calls this trophy missable, but treat the hunt itself as a set-piece and save before you start it. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); side-activity grouping per FullSweep.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep trophy list

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full Collectible Card sets. The key word is sets: scattered singles do not count until a set is finished, so hunt set by set instead of grabbing random cards across the map. Cards are classic open-world collectibles — expect them on rooftops, in interiors and at landmarks — and they feed the completion checklist for A Long Road. Use this tracker's collectibles filter to plan a sweep route per district, and mark a set done only when its last card is in hand. Sources: official description and count (Exophase / PSNProfiles); collectibles grouping per FullSweep and Techtroduce.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep; Techtroduce

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use WAiNK at 100 different locations. This is a coverage trophy, not a skill trophy: the counter rewards travelling, so weave WAiNK spots into everything else you do — story travel, strand missions, exploration for The Goodtime State — instead of leaving 100 stops for one endgame session. Keep a rough district tally in this tracker and finish one district's spots before moving on, so a missed location stands out instead of blending into a statewide guess; if you finish the story well short of 100, sweep the map region by region, because locations, like the stunts and cards, overlap with the 100% checklist. Sources: official description and the 100-location count (Exophase / PSNProfiles).
trophies.sources: Official list + 100 count (Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete any 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's short-form objectives scattered through free play and activities, so the natural route is breadth: try everything once for Master of None, and challenges will complete along the way. If you reach the endgame short of 50, open the in-game challenge list, sort by what is nearly done, and close those out first — the trophy counts completions, not categories. Sources: official description and count (Exophase / PSNProfiles); challenge role in the 100% checklist per GTA Culture summary via Heyday.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); Heyday completion summary

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, raise a 4-star wanted level, then lose it and fully escape — the stars must actually clear, not just pause. Plan the escape before the crime: a fast car, a route with tunnels, alleys or a vehicle swap, and distance from the search zone. Four stars brings helicopters and aggressive units, so break line of sight early and keep moving. The partner requirement is the part players miss: do it during free play with your partner present, not solo. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles).
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner, keeping a wanted level alive the whole time — if the stars fully clear between shops, the chain breaks. Scout the run first in calm conditions: pick three shops close together on one street and drive the route between them once, so the real run is memory, not improvisation. Then rob them fast, and drive directly between them; you want the heat to persist, not escalate out of control, so avoid cop kills that spike the response. Have the escape route for after the third shop planned in advance, because only then do you want to disappear. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles).
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. Discovery registers as you encounter and drive the game's vehicle roster, so variety is everything: swap cars often, visit rich districts, docks, airfields and rural roads, and never drive past a model you have not sat in. This pairs naturally with On the Spot — register eligible vehicles in the Scooter Bros app while you are discovering them, and two counters advance at once. Late-game, the in-game vehicle list shows what your garage of discoveries still lacks. Sources: official description and count (Exophase / PSNProfiles).
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Drop 5 enemies inside one Combat Focus activation. Set the moment up rather than hoping for it: find a spot where five or more enemies cluster — a gang operation or a busy robbery gone loud — top up your focus meter, line up your targets, then trigger Combat Focus and work left to right without wasting shots. Put your back to a wall or doorway before you trigger it, so all five targets sit inside one field of view — Combat Focus punishes turning to hunt for a target more than it punishes a missed shot. If you get four, do not force it; reposition, rebuild the meter and engineer another cluster. Shooting Range practice for The Shootist pays off directly here. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles).
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the airport — in plain terms, get airborne (or otherwise leave) from the airport in a way the airport did not intend. Do the story mission VCIA Takedown first (Hi-Jacked) so you know the layout, then return in free play: reach an aircraft, get in, and take off despite the response. Expect an instant wanted level, so commit to the takeoff roll and climb out rather than fighting on the tarmac. The precise trigger is one of the list's vaguer descriptions; the official wording is the requirement, and this reading of it is this guide's own. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); cross-reference with Hi-Jacked in the official list.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); cross-reference within the official list

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The official description is a joke, not a method — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' — and Rhinos are the game's tanks. The honest guide is this: the trophy is tied to the Rhino tank somehow, and no source checked for this guide confirms the exact trigger, so treat any specific step you read elsewhere as unconfirmed. The practical approach: when you first encounter a Rhino (high wanted levels and military responses are the usual route), get in one and survive in it, and watch for the pop. It is listed here as hidden with a deliberately vague description, the classic shape of a secret one-off trophy. Sources: official description, quoted in full (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer notes hidden-trophy methods still being confirmed.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap caveat

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store cleanly: get in, take the goods and get out without being detected. Scout the store first — entrances, staff positions, sightlines — approach quietly, avoid cameras and witnesses, and leave by the least-watched exit. If you are spotted, do not finish the robbery out of stubbornness; walk away, let the area reset, and run it again undetected. Detection is the only failure state, so patience is the whole strategy. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles).
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape each time — a robbery only counts when you get away, so the escape is half the job. Work banks one at a time with the heist discipline The Cartel Heist taught: full armour, a fast getaway car parked smart, and a route rehearsed before you go loud. Five separate successful vault robberies are needed, not one bank five ways, so spread them across the map and tick each bank off here as you clear it. Sources: official description and count (Exophase / PSNProfiles); robbery grouping per Push Square coverage via LeonidaUnlocked.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); Push Square via LeonidaUnlocked

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armoured truck and escape with the take. Armoured trucks are moving targets: intercept one on a quiet stretch, disable it or force the doors with the tools the game gives you, grab the cash fast and be gone before the response converges. A failed escape means no trophy even if you opened the truck, so prioritise the getaway vehicle and route over squeezing extra seconds at the truck. One successful truck is enough. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles).
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore the whole state: the official list's count puts Leonida at 52 areas, and every one must be visited. This trophy completes itself if you are thorough — story missions, strands, stunts, cards and WAiNK stops spread you across the map — so save the deliberate sweep for last, when the remaining dark patches on your map are obvious. Coastal and island areas are the usual stragglers; take a boat and close them out. Exploration also feeds the 100% checklist. Sources: official description and the 52-area count (Exophase / PSNProfiles list data); EGamers list summary.
trophies.sources: Official list + 52 count (Exophase / PSNProfiles); EGamers

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one Illegal Operation run by each gang — 9 gangs in the official list's count. One robbery per gang is enough; you do not need to clear every operation on the map for this trophy (though operations feed the completion checklist). Vary your approach by territory, expect heavier resistance than a shop robbery, and record which gangs you have hit in this tracker, because the game will not hand you a tidy per-gang checklist. Gang operations are also a reliable place to set up Gunslinger's five-enemy Combat Focus. Sources: official description and the 9-gang count (Exophase / PSNProfiles list data).
trophies.sources: Official list + 9 count (Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This is one of the list's small scene trophies: go to Ocean Beach, find the bar or cocktail prompt the location offers, and take the moment. The ellipsis in the official name is printed as PlayStation publishes it. Scene trophies like this are easy to walk past for 200 hours, so if you are passing Ocean Beach at any point in the story, stop for two minutes and bank it. Sources: official description and location (Exophase / PSNProfiles).
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom, in a vehicle, through the glass — 'in classic style', as the official description puts it. Enter a vehicle showroom, get into one of the display cars, and drive it out through the showroom frontage rather than the door. It is a deliberate homage moment, so any showroom with a car you can enter should do; if the first showroom's cars are locked down, try another. Expect a wanted level afterwards, and a short escape. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles).
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Go to the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley and bowl — the trophy's wording, 'Follow-through', points at actually playing the bowling activity there rather than just visiting. The curly apostrophe in the official name is as PlayStation publishes it. Bowling is also one of the activity types, so a game here can count toward Master of None at the same time. Play the activity through to its end rather than quitting mid-frame. Sources: official description and venue name (Exophase / PSNProfiles); activity grouping per FullSweep.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); FullSweep

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: Another deliberately vague hidden description: 'A partnership with mass appeal.' No source checked for this guide confirms the exact trigger, and this guide will not invent one. The wording points at something done together with your partner that draws a crowd or an audience, so the practical advice is: do partner activities and public set-pieces as they appear, especially anything involving performing, showing off or gathering attention with your partner present, and watch for the pop. If you finish everything else first, revisit partner activities in busy public places. Sources: official description, quoted in full (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer notes some hidden-trophy methods are still being confirmed.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap caveat

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make choices — lots of them. The official description is minimal, but the count carried with the list shows PlayStation tracking this one toward 500, which makes it a cumulative counter, not a single moment: dialogue choices, mission decisions and branching interactions across the whole game are the sensible reading. You cannot grind it in one spot; you earn it by playing everything and choosing whenever the game asks. Keeping a pre-finale save (see the gold story trophy) is still wise in case a late choice matters to you, but the counter itself only grows by playing. Sources: official description and the tracked count in the list data (Exophase / PSNProfiles).
trophies.sources: Official list + tracked count (Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: The description — 'Second time's the charm' — describes a shape, not a place: fail at something once, then succeed at it on the retry. No source checked for this guide pins down which activity it belongs to, so do not trust any guide that states one as fact. It will most likely pop on its own during a long platinum run, the first time you retry a challenge, race or attempt and succeed. If it has not popped by the clean-up stage, deliberately retry activities you previously failed until it does. Sources: official description, quoted in full (Exophase / PSNProfiles).
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange. The official description ('What the hell just happened?') is the whole brief: this is the list's oddity trophy, tied to some strange event or sighting somewhere in Leonida. KeenGamer's roadmap is candid that this hidden trophy's unlock method was still unconfirmed when it published, and this guide stays equally candid — anyone naming an exact spot as fact is guessing. Explore off the beaten path (it pairs with The Goodtime State's full-map sweep), investigate odd encounters when they appear, and expect it when you least expect it. Sources: official description, quoted in full (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer lists the method as unconfirmed.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock a person down with a melee drive-by: swing a melee attack from a moving vehicle and connect with a pedestrian or enemy so they go down like a bowling pin — the name is the joke and the method at once. Line up a slow pass rather than a high-speed one, time the swing as you pass, and do it somewhere the wanted level is easy to shed afterwards. KeenGamer notes the precise method was still being confirmed at publication, so if a clean hit does not register, vary speed and weapon until the drive-by melee connects properly. Sources: official description (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer method caveat.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts, cumulatively. Marked Bills come from the game's dirtier income streams, so route them through your laundering contacts whenever you hold them instead of sitting on them, and this counter climbs steadily through the story. It is a marathon number, not a single score: if you reach the endgame short, keep running the robbery and operation loop (Pest Control, Maximum Withdrawal) and launder everything until the total crosses $250,000. Sources: official description and amount (Exophase / PSNProfiles); EGamers list table.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); EGamers

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops, in total. It is cumulative and counts ordinary play — weapons, ammo, armour, clothes, vehicle work, food — so most players cross it naturally during a platinum run. Do not hoard cash out of habit in the early game; buying the gear that makes other trophies easier is spending that counts twice. If you are short at clean-up, garages and high-end shops (see Little Boxes) will close the gap quickly. Sources: official description and amount (Exophase / PSNProfiles).
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles)

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy every garage property — 8 of them, per the count carried with the official list. Garages are bought with in-game cash as they become available, so this is a money trophy wearing a property trophy's clothes: keep your income streams (robberies, operations, laundering) running and buy each garage as it unlocks rather than saving for a single spree. Owning garages also gives your discovered vehicles somewhere to live, which supports Whip It Good. Sources: official description and the 8-garage count (Exophase / PSNProfiles list data); KeenGamer roadmap.
trophies.sources: Official list + 8 count (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Whenever you get into a vehicle you intend to keep or have just discovered, register it in the app before you abandon it; ten registrations is a small number if you build the habit early and an annoying scavenger hunt if you leave it. Pair it with Whip It Good — discover broadly, register the keepers — and both counters finish in the same drives. Sources: official description and count (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap.
trophies.sources: Official list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); KeenGamer roadmap
